signal: EliseAI raised a $250M Series E in August 2025 at a $2.2B valuation led by a16z and Bessemer, and grew to roughly 600 employees by mid-2026.

email.body1:
Sergey, saw EliseAI raised its $250M Series E at a $2.2B valuation and is now near 600 people.

Growth that fast usually means more buying signals than the team can action before they go stale, and that latency quietly caps pipeline. Our AI SDR turns signals into researched, personalized outreach automatically: 3-5x more meetings per rep, no new headcount.

I built a signal play for EliseAI off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Sergey, quick follow-up for EliseAI.

At post-Series-E scale, pipeline usually leaks in the lag between a signal firing and a rep touching the account. Tightening that loop is a bigger lever than more headcount, and our best practices alone lift response rates 50-70%.

Worth 15 minutes? I'll walk you through a teardown of your current outbound, three things I'd change, and how to cut signal-to-action latency without adding reps.
email.body3:
Sergey, last bit of proof for EliseAI.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how EliseAI's reply rate likely compares to other high-growth AI startups. Want to hop on a quick call and I'll walk you through it?
email.body4:
Sergey, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If cutting signal-to-action latency isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Scaling RevOps right after a raise is its own kind of busy, and timing matters.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to a RevOps motion? I'll tailor it to EliseAI either way.
